text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing its behavior. The main goal is to make code easier to read, understand, and maintain. For example, you might rename confusing variables, break a long function into smaller ones, or remove repeated code. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs; the program should work exactly the same after it. However, refactoring is important because it reduces technical debt. Over time, messy code becomes harder to update, so regular refactoring helps teams work faster and avoid bigger problems in the future.
